overview: Graph-of-Agents (GoA) is a graph-based framework for multi-agent LLM collaboration that selects relevant agents via node sampling using model cards and a meta-LLM, constructs directed edges based on inter-agent relevance scoring, performs bidirectional message passing (source-to-target then target-to-source) for response refinement, and aggregates final answers through graph pooling (max or mean), evaluated on multi-domain and domain-specific benchmarks against existing multi-agent baselines.

modules.name: Model Card Extraction and Management
modules.description: Extracts and structures model card metadata from Hugging Face README files into standardized summaries covering domain, task specialization, parameter size, and special features. Maintains a model card dictionary mapping each LLM agent to its concise card representation for downstream node sampling.

modules.name: Node Sampling via Meta-LLM
modules.description: Implements the agent selection mechanism where a general-purpose meta-LLM takes the input query and the model card dictionary as input and selects the top-k most relevant agents. Outputs the selected agent subset Vs from the full agent pool V.

modules.name: Initial Response Generation
modules.description: Prompts each selected agent to generate an initial structured response (with reasoning, answer, and confidence level in JSON format) to the input query. Collects and stores the initial response set R for subsequent edge sampling and message passing.

modules.name: Edge Sampling and Adjacency Construction
modules.description: Constructs the weighted directed adjacency matrix governing agent communication. Each agent scores all other agents' responses (excluding self) with scores summing to 1.0, computes per-agent relevance scores by summing incoming scores, prunes agents below threshold τ, and normalizes neighbor scores to produce the adjacency matrix A where Aji represents the influence of agent i on agent j.

modules.name: Source-to-Target Message Passing
modules.description: Implements the first message passing step where information flows from higher-ranked (source) agents to lower-ranked (target) agents. For each target node, concatenates neighboring source responses weighted by adjacency entries, feeds the augmented context to the target LLM for response refinement, producing updated responses R'_j for all target nodes.

modules.name: Target-to-Source Message Passing
modules.description: Implements the reverse message passing step where refined responses from target nodes are propagated back to source nodes. Each source node receives updated responses from its neighbors and refines its own output accordingly, producing final refined responses R''_i. Enables source agents to incorporate consensus from their neighborhood.

modules.name: Graph Pooling for Answer Aggregation
modules.description: Aggregates refined agent responses into a single unified answer. Implements two variants: (1) Max-pooling selecting the response from the agent with the highest number of incoming source edges, and (2) Mean-pooling applying weighted averaging of all refined responses using relevance scores, then passing through the meta-LLM for final synthesis.

modules.name: GoA End-to-End Pipeline Orchestrator
modules.description: Coordinates the full GoA workflow from query input to final answer output, sequencing node sampling, initial response generation, edge sampling, bidirectional message passing, and graph pooling. Manages state transitions between pipeline stages and handles the complete forward pass of the framework.

modules.name: Benchmark Data Loader and Preprocessor
modules.description: Loads and preprocesses all evaluation benchmarks including MMLU, MMLU-Pro, GPQA (multi-domain) and MATH, HumanEval, MedMCQA (domain-specific). Implements stratified sampling for large benchmarks (50 samples per category for MMLU, 150 per category for MMLU-Pro), format conversion to unified query structure, and answer extraction logic for different task types (multiple-choice, code generation, mathematical expression).

modules.name: Evaluation Metrics Computation
modules.description: Computes all evaluation metrics used in the paper: accuracy for multiple-choice benchmarks (MMLU, MMLU-Pro, GPQA, MedMCQA), mathematical correctness for MATH, pass@1 rate for HumanEval code generation, and overall average performance. Handles task-specific answer parsing and comparison logic.

modules.name: Multi-Agent Baseline Implementations
modules.description: Implements all comparison baselines: Debate (symmetric multi-agent debate), Self-Consistency (majority voting across multiple samples), Refine (iterative self-refinement), ReConcile (confidence-based consensus), Mixture-of-Agents (MoA with many-to-one aggregation across layers), and Self-MoA. Each baseline operates on the same agent pool for fair comparison.

modules.name: Ablation Study Framework
modules.description: Implements controlled ablation experiments including: reversing message passing direction (target-to-source first), removing target-to-source step, removing source-to-target step, disabling edge scoring (uniform Aij=1), varying top-k agent selection count, and adjusting edge pruning threshold τ. Provides structured comparison of each variant against the full GoA configuration.

modules.name: Efficiency and Cost Analysis
modules.description: Measures and reports computational efficiency metrics: total number of LLM API calls, cumulative token usage (input plus output), and end-to-end latency in seconds per query. Enables comparison between GoA and baselines on cost-effectiveness, supporting the efficiency claims of the graph-based selective approach versus full-pool methods.

modules.name: Prompt Template Management
modules.description: Manages all prompt templates used across the GoA pipeline: model card extraction prompts, node sampling selection prompts, initial response generation prompts (with JSON output formatting), edge sampling scoring prompts, source-to-target and target-to-source refinement prompts (with relevance level annotations), and graph pooling synthesis prompts. Ensures consistency and reproducibility of prompt engineering.

modules.name: Configuration and Experiment Management
modules.description: Handles YAML/JSON-based configuration for all hyperparameters (top-k, threshold τ, pooling strategy, agent pool definition, benchmark selection), experiment tracking across runs, result aggregation for multi-benchmark evaluation tables, and automated generation of performance comparison tables matching the paper's format (single-agent, multi-agent, GoA variants). Supports scaling experiments with different model families (e.g., gpt-4o).
